 Brandon Williams (hamstring) will not return to Monday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 Williams played less than two minutes in the first quarter of Monday’s game before leaving the game with a left hamstring injury. LJ Cryer has moved into the back end of the Warriors’ rotation and could stick there for a bit if Williams misses time.

 De’Anthony Melton amassed 16 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans. 
 Melton was one of four Warriors to make at least four three-pointers in Monday’s blowout victory. With Brandon Williams suffering a hamstring injury in the first quarter, Melton is one Warrior whose minutes may increase if Williams misses time. Currently a player who should be rostered in deep leagues, some managers in 12-team leagues may be willing to roll the dice on Melton in the short term. 
 Gary Payton 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Gary Payton II (calf) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Magic. 
 Payton most recently played 10 minutes off the bench in Thursday’s win over the Heat. His absence wouldn’t affect fantasy basketball, but De’Anthony Melton and Brandon Williams could absorb the minutes. 
 Will Richard 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Will Richard started on Thursday and finished with 10 points (4-of-6 FGs), one rebound, two assists, one block and two three-pointers against the Heat. 
 Richard got the starting nod for the second straight game and for the third time this season. Multiple players have filled out the fifth starting spot with Jimmy Butler III (knee) sidelined to start the year. Richard only played 16 minutes in this game, with Georges Niang and Brandon Williams each surpassing 20 minutes and scoring in double figures. Richard may continue to start, but he isn’t worth adding off the waiver wire.

 Williams is available after missing Monday’s win over the Suns. He’ll provide perimeter depth off the bench, which limits his fantasy ceiling.

 Guard 
 #12 
 Brandon Williams (quad) has been ruled out against the Suns on Monday. 
 Williams will be unavailable on the second night of this back-to-back. He has been a reliable source of offense for the Warriors this season as the backup point guard. Gary Payton II and Will Richard should take on extra minutes in his absence.

 Guard 
 #12 
 Brandon Williams (quad) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 Williams is dealing with a left quad contusion. He’s provided a spark off the bench so far this year, but his potential absence won’t impact fantasy basketball. 
 Brandon Williams 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #12 
 Brandon Williams tallied 17 points (7-of-11 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one block and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Clippers. 
 Although he didn’t get the starting nod for Sunday’s game, Williams was one of the Warriors’ available guards who took advantage of Stephen Curry’s absence. He shot 5-for-8 from the field in the first half, scoring 12 of his 17 points. Williams wasn’t as productive in the second half, but this was a solid night for a player whose contract won’t be fully guaranteed until January 10. The Warriors play three games next week, starting with the Suns on Monday. 
 Brandon Williams 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #12 
 Brandon Williams (back) is available for Monday’s game against the Nuggets. 
 Initially listed as probable for Monday’s game, Williams is now available. Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski are available after sitting out Saturday, so Williams will come off the bench. 
 Brandon Williams 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #12 
 Brandon Williams (back) and Charles Bassey (knee) are probable for Monday’s game against the Nuggets. 
 Bassey made his first appearance of the season in Saturday’s loss to the Suns, playing 13 minutes off the bench. However, the Warriors missed Draymond Green and Al Horford, and both will be available on Monday. Bassey’s playing time is likely to decrease. As for Williams, if cleared for Monday’s game, he’ll come off the bench after scoring 20 points as a spot starter on Saturday. His chances of sticking in the rotation are greater than Bassey’s, even though the Warriors will also get Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski back. 
 Brandon Williams 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #12 
 Brandon Williams tallied 20 points (5-of-10 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Suns. 
 With Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski sitting out the second game of Golden State’s back-to-back, Williams and Will Richard (11 points, one assist, two steals, one block and three three-pointers) were inserted into the starting lineup on Saturday. After shooting 4-of-17 in Golden State’s first two games, Williams was much more efficient against the Suns. His fantasy value will depend on the schedule going forward, and the Warriors end their four-game Week 2 with another back-to-back.

 Derik Queen notched 16 points (4-of-8 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), four rebounds and three blocks in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 Queen did most of his damage offensively in the second quarter, scoring eight of his 16 points. However, of greater importance to fantasy managers may be the three blocks, a new season-high and two shy of the second-year forward/center’s career high. However, his defense remains a work in progress, even with the blocks recorded on Monday. While Queen has been a consistently productive option for fantasy managers, the defensive issues are why he’s averaging 22 minutes per game and not more.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jeremiah Fears accounted for 11 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, eight assists, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 Fears led the Pelicans with eight assists, but he also recorded six turnovers in Monday’s 138-87 defeat. This was one of his poorer performances of the season, and the Pelicans not having Trey Murphy or Zion Williamson didn’t help either. Fears will look to bounce back on Wednesday when the Pelicans host the Nets. That should be a better matchup for him than the red-hot Warriors were.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Dejounte Murray tallied 12 points (5-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 The Pelicans didn’t have Trey Murphy or Zion Williamson on Monday, and those absences were certainly felt. Murray shot a solid percentage from the field and led the Pelicans starters in scoring, but it wasn’t enough when the Warriors knocked down 21 three-pointers. Murray has been close to a top-50 player in nine-cat formats, but it’s fair to wonder if his presence in the lineup has limited Jeremiah Fears’ fantasy ceiling. That’s something to watch as the season progresses.

 Yaxel Lendeborg produced 23 points (8-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
 Lendeborg continues to shine for the Warriors, making all four of his three-point attempts on Monday. The rookie forward has scored at least 20 points in six of 11 games and is considered by many to be one of the early favorites for Rookie of the Year. The Warriors play two more games this week, at Houston and San Antonio, so we’ll learn a bit more about Lendeborg in games of that magnitude.

 Brandin Podziemski amassed 25 points (10-of-19 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
 Podziemski shot 5-of-11 from beyond the arc on Monday, a season high for three-pointers in a game for the fourth-year guard. Even better for fantasy managers, Podz recorded a complete stat line, his third in as many games. Based on his ADP, Podziemski wasn’t expected to be a top-100 player this season. However, while it is early, he’s been a top-75 player in nine-cat formats.

 Stephen Curry tallied 25 points (6-of-10 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
 Curry only played 21 minutes in Monday’s blowout victory, none in the fourth quarter. That’s all the time he needed to notch another career milestone, as the Warriors guard moved past DeMar DeRozan into 16th place on the NBA’s all-time scoring list. Thus far, Curry’s production has exceeded his preseason ADP by a safe distance, as he’s been a top-5 player in nine-cat formats. The Warriors end their week with games against the Rockets and Spurs, two teams that should offer up greater resistance than the Pelicans did.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Maxime Raynaud (knee) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Magic. 
 Working his way back from a right patellar subluxation suffered during the preseason, Raynaud was to be re-evaluated early this week. That did not happen on Monday, but the Kings are listing the second-year center out for Tuesday night. Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell have been providing depth at center when Domantas Sabonis is not on the floor.

 Dillon Brooks finished Monday’s loss to the Spurs with seven points (3-of-14 FGs), four rebounds and one three-pointer.
 While Devin Booker scored 32 points, no other Suns starter scored more than seven in Monday’s 122-96 defeat. Brooks had an especially rough night, as he shot 2-of-12 from inside the three-point line. While he managed a few rebounds, his poor shooting was compounded by a lack of assists and defensive stats. Brooks will look to bounce back on Tuesday against the Clippers.
